response: Yes, many colorectal cancers are due to missed adenomas. Adenomas are precancerous polyps in the colon or rectum that can develop into cancer over time if not removed. Studies have shown that a significant proportion of colorectal cancers arise from adenomas that were missed during previous colonoscopies or other screening tests. It's estimated that up to 60% of colorectal cancers may be due to missed adenomas, highlighting the importance of high-quality colonoscopy and thorough polyp removal to prevent colorectal cancer.
